players.name: António João Pereira de Albuquerque Tavares da Silva
António João Pereira de Albuquerque Tavares da Silva

1.headline: Haaland captaincies everywhere, João Pedro doing the heavy lifting and Woolly arriving with a 21-point boot to smash Turf Less
1.introduction: Gameweek 1 arrives and, as ever, the Super 8s served up its usual mix of sensible picks, baffling captaincies and someone entirely forgetful about their bench. There were slim margins, a 21-point spanking, and a handful of managers already nursing regrets they’ll blame on 'bad luck' in the pub.

matches.title: Richard (Rich) 56 v Prince Majid Rd FC (Rami) 57 — Rami nicks it by one
matches.text: Rami edged Rich by a single point, because of course the first week would produce a one-point thriller. Both managers leaned on Bruno as captain (both got 4 effective points), and João Pedro popped up with 11 for both sides — the man doing the heavy lifting across the league. Rich will rue the low returns from Haaland (only 2 points) but at least his bench had some useless-looking points to stare at. Rami’s winning margin: a perfectly polite 1 point and nothing to see here except smugness in Riyadh.

matches.title: Humorous Name United (Rob) 72 v Roped in again (Paul) 71 — a classic one-point cliff-hanger
matches.text: Rob beat Paul by one point in the highest-scoring match of the week (143 combined). Rob’s Bruno captaincy returned 4 effective points; Paul’s Haaland captain also produced exactly 4 — you could call it captaincy symmetry, if you were being charitable. João Pedro again chipped in with 11, proving he’ll appear in awkward places this season. Paul scored 71 and still lost, which is the sort of nonsense that makes you check the app twice and threaten to delete the league.

matches.title: Change Name FC (David) 67 v Bielsa's Babes (Patrick) 76 — Patrick clears the bar
matches.text: Patrick put 76 on the board and comfortably beat David by nine. Patrick’s squad spread the points around (Benjamin White 11, João Pedro 11), so despite a modest Haaland return his total was the week’s highest. David also had a solid 67 — respectable, but not quite enough to cope with Patrick’s balanced assault. Patrick is currently top of the league; enjoy it while it lasts.

matches.title: el Guapo (Tom) 47 v BeLucky Again (Kev) 51 — Tom’s bench betrayed him
matches.text: Tom posted the week’s lowest score (47) and will be staring longingly at his bench: Granit Xhaka had 9 but was left unused. Tom captained Haaland (double) for a meek 4 effective points — the captaincy didn’t do its job and his unused bench did. Kev’s Ødegaard (11) and João Pedro (11) did the job quietly; 51 was enough to nick the away win. Tom, who loves Spurs, might call this 'Spursy' — we'll call it an absolute shambles.

matches.title: FC Dangerous (Watson) 50 v Seattle Scorchers (Andrew) 50 — honours even
matches.text: Rob and Andrew drew 50 apiece, the narrowest possible result. Both captained Haaland and both received the same paltry captain return (4 effective points), so no one got any bragging rights. Ødegaard again chipped in with 11 for Rob; James Trafford’s 9 for Andrew was a decent goalkeeper effort. A tidy, low-drama stalemate — perfectly suited to Monday morning text messages that read 'could've been worse.'

matches.title: ChampagneSuperRovers (James) 55 v Atletico Waspo (Foz) 59 — Foster squeezes past
matches.text: Foz beat James by four. João Pedro and Iliman Ndiaye featured where needed, and Ben’s Joao 11 was decisive. James had Granit Xhaka 9 and other decent returns but came up short. Nothing dramatic, just the kind of small margins that will have James tinkering with his team all week for no real reason.

matches.title: Woolbrohampton (Woolly) 71 v Turf Less (Martyn) 50 — Ben hits the big hammer
matches.text: Woolly delivered the biggest winning margin of the week (21 points) to put Martyn in the kind of hole only matchday banter can fill. Martyn’s Cole Palmer managed 13 — the best individual score in the league — but it wasn’t nearly enough. Ben had João Pedro 11 and a tidy spread of contributions to reach 71. Martyn, a Burnley fan, took a proper hiding — which feels unfairly apt somehow.

awards.text: Top score 76 despite a mediocre-captain Haaland. Patrick’s spread of points (White 11, João Pedro 11, Ødegaard 11) made this look effortless — smugness currently included in the prize.
Tom scored the week’s low (47) and left Granit Xhaka’s 9 on the bench. That bench looks at him now like an ex you ignored at the bar.
Biggest margin (71-50). Ben demolished Turf Less and ensured his name will be mentioned in bar-room gloating for at least 48 hours.
72-71 over Paul in the highest-scoring match. Winning a shootout like that is the fantasy equivalent of stealing sandwiches from under someone’s nose.

1.table_commentary: Using H2H points and total FPL as the tie‑breaker, the league looks like this: Patrick’s Bielsa's Babes top the pile, with Humorous Name United (Rob) breathing down his neck in second and Woolly’s Woolbrohampton third. Foz’s Atletico Waspo and Rami’s Prince Majid Rd FC sit comfortably inside the top six alongside Kev’s BeLucky Again. Mid‑table is the pair of 50-50s — Watson and Crystal — having shared the spoils, while Paul and Rich start with big scores but one loss and slip into the lower half. David, James, Tom and Martyn all have work to do; Tom’s bench shenanigans mean he’s currently bottom of that unhappy quartet. All very early days, but already plenty to argue about in the WhatsApp group.

preview.fixture: Prince Majid Rd FC (Rami) v Woolbrohampton (Woolly)
preview.text: Rami hosts Woolly next — a test for Rami after his one-point win. Ben arrives after a 21-point smash and will fancy himself, while Rami will try to convince us his squad-building is not just money and a VPN. Expect João Pedro to be in the middle of it again.

Martyn needs a response after that 21-point hiding, and James will be quietly confident after a tidy away showing. Martyn’s Cole Palmer was excellent and he’ll hope for more of the same; James will want to avoid the small margins that cost him against Foz.

preview.fixture: Bielsa's Babes (Patrick) v Humorous Name United (Rob)
preview.text: Leeds-on-Leeds, which is fun for the two of them and annoying for everyone else — both are sitting high early. Patrick top of the table faces Rob who narrowly won his opener; whichever Leeds fan wins, expect at least one other manager to complain about how much those two ‘moan about fixtures’. Should be spicy.

1.closing: That’s your Gameweek 1 digest: close calls, a brutal thrashing and several captaincies already asking for therapy. Get your teams right — and if you left good players on the bench, don’t bother apologising; just promise a transfer and then do nothing.

2.headline: The Bruno Bug: Double-captains everywhere and still somehow not enough for everyone
2.introduction: Gameweek 2 served up enough double-captain hysteria to make a telemarketer’s head spin. Bruno Borges Fernandes was the unofficial mascot of the weekend — several managers slapped the armband on him and watched 46 points appear like applause. There were high scores (hello 115), a few wasted benches (looking at you, Pascal Groß), and a draw so symmetric it felt like two managers had shared a single brain cell.

matches.title: Prince Majid Rd FC (Rami) 90 — Woolbrohampton (Ben) 104
matches.text: Rami double-captained Bruno and enjoyed 46 magic points from him — which is impressive, shame it wasn’t enough. Woolly did the exact same trick (also 46 from Bruno) and still edged it by 14 thanks to contributions across the pitch: Haaland 13, João Pedro 9 and a steady supporting cast. Bonus bit of cruelty for Ben: Pascal Groß scored 13 on his bench and went unused — the kind of bench punctuality that keeps statisticians awake at night.

matches.title: Turf Less (Martyn) 85 — ChampagneSuperRovers (James) 103
matches.text: Dunne’s Haaland hand (double-capped for 26) proved decisive as ChampagneSuperRovers finished well clear. Martyn tried a cheeky double on Cole Palmer (14) but it couldn’t close the gap; Bruno again popped up with 23 for Turf Less but, as the scoreboard shows, one big name doesn’t win the whole thing.

matches.title: Atletico Waspo (Ben F) 99 — FC Dangerous (Watson) 108
matches.text: Foz’s side hit 99 despite a big 26 from his own Haaland — but Watson’s FC Dangerous had the better balance. Watson’s double-captain bet on Bukayo Saka paid out (22) and Rayan Cherki’s 14 added weight; that was enough to nick a nine-point win.

matches.title: Seattle Scorchers (Andrew) 99 — el Guapo (Tom) 76
matches.text: Crystal was too hot for Tom this week. Seattle leaned on the Bruno double again (46) and added tidy returns elsewhere to build a comfortable 23-point cushion. Tom’s double-Haaland (26) couldn’t paper over the cracks — a reminder that even a doubled superstar needs colleagues who deliver.

matches.title: BeLucky Again (Kev) 82 — Change Name FC (David W) 100
matches.text: Dave cruised to three points as Change Name FC hit a century. David’s Haaland double (26) combined with Bruno’s usual 23 to outscore Kevin’s decent but insufficient haul. Kevin did have Haaland as his double as well (26), so this one came down to the rest of the XI — and David’s supporting cast simply did more.

matches.title: Bielsa's Babes (Patrick) 115 — Humorous Name United (Rob W) 115
matches.text: A one-in-a-thousand sort of result: identical 115s and a shared scalp of the week. Both Patrick and Rob W double-captained Bruno for 46 and both reaped identical returns elsewhere — a truly symmetrical draw. They also share the honour of the week’s highest score, which makes the trophy cabinet rather awkward.

matches.title: Roped in again (Paul) 92 — Richard (Rich) 108
matches.text: Rich’s Richard took three points in comfortable fashion. Once again Bruno shows up big where it counts — Rich double-capped Bruno for 46 and it sliced through Paul’s otherwise respectable return (Paul’s Haaland double gave 26 but the rest of the side didn’t quite match it).

awards.text: Both Patrick and Rob W double-capped Bruno and ended up with identical 115s. When the virus spreads, it spreads symmetrically.
Ben had Pascal Groß scoring 13 on his bench — brilliant work by Pascal, tragic timing by Ben.
Rami double-capped Bruno for 46 and still lost. Brave, committed and ultimately heartbreaking.
Lowest score of the week at 76. Tom’s double-Haaland got 26, but the rest of the XI looked like they’d been sent home early.

2.table_commentary: Woolly’s Woolbrohampton sits top with the perfect six H2H points and a healthy 175 FPL points — unbeaten and smug. Behind him is Paddy’s Bielsa's Babes on four points, narrowly ahead of Rob’s Humorous Name United thanks to the official tie-breaker of total FPL points (191 vs 187). There’s a four-way cluster on four points in total if you include Watson and Crystal, but the tie-breakers shuffle their order. Mid-table is congested: several teams on three H2H points after trading wins and losses in the opening pair of weeks. At the other end, Paul (Roped in again), Bradshaw (Turf Less) and Tom (el Guapo) are yet to find a point from two matches and will be sharpening transfer knives.

preview.fixture: Humorous Name United vs Prince Majid Rd FC (event 3)
preview.text: Rob W faces Rami next. Both managers are dangerous in different ways — Rob already has that 115 under his belt, Rami will be licking his wounds after a Bruno double that didn’t quite win. Expect more Bruno-related decisions and a tight encounter on paper.
Dave hosts Rich in what looks like a revenge/reaffirmation tie. Both came away with wins this week, so it could be a toss-up of who’s got the deeper bench and who resists wasting Pascal Groß again.

Top-of-the-table Woolly welcomes Crystal. Ben is unbeaten and will fancy his chances, but Andrew’s Seattle have shown they can pile on the points when Bruno turns up. Could be the first heavyweight clash of the mini-season.

2.closing: That’s your lot for Gameweek 2 — plenty of double-captain drama, a couple of wasted benches and a tie so neat it could’ve been scheduled. See you next week; start deciding who gets the armband before the Bruno contagion spreads any further.
